C-FIX-MUSIC-START-RACE.Summary: Fix the two defects the first on-device run of the music channel exposed: a start race that builds two players for one track, and a life-cycle path that restarts the track instead of resuming it.
C-FIX-MUSIC-START-RACE.Problem: Running the app on macOS with temporary logging inside the music player produced every line twice — "prepared assets/music/almost-floating.mp3", "playing ... at 0.0" and "faded in to 0.25" each appeared twice for a single launch. Two causes compound. First, AudioPlayersMusicPlayer._playerFor checks the player map and only publishes the new player after `await setSource(...)` completes, so two callers arriving before that await finishes both miss the map entry and each builds a player: one track, two players, the music audible in two voices. Second, nothing prevents those two callers: MusicService.load() starts the track and the very first AppLifecycleState.resumed notification, delivered right after the observer is registered, starts it again. The same life-cycle path has a third, quieter defect: returning to the foreground calls _start(), which stops and resumes, so the track begins from the beginning rather than continuing — wrong for a channel whose whole purpose is to fall silent and come back. Neither the unit tests nor the analyzer can see any of this: they do not run two concurrent callers, and they do not listen.

Goals.Goal: Make player creation single-instance even under concurrent callers, by sharing the pending load rather than the finished player.
Make starting idempotent: asking for the track that is already playing must not restart it.
Keep the position across foreground changes: pause when the app leaves, resume when it returns, and reserve stop for switching the channel off.
Pin all three behaviours with tests, so the holes this slipped through are closed.

Constraints.Constraint: The public shape of MusicService does not change: same enabled, volume, load, setEnabled, dispose and prefs key. This is a defect fix, not a redesign.
The interface-sound channel, the header control and the assets are untouched.
Tests stay device-free and fast: no real audio, no waiting on the fade.
Pause must not be confused with stop: disable resets the track, a foreground change does not.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No change to the fade length, the volumes or the rotation order.
No new preferences, no track picker, no changes to the header menu.
No attempt to also rework how the app handles life cycle elsewhere; only the music channel is in scope.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: MusicPlayer exposes pause and resume beside stop, and AudioPlayersMusicPlayer implements them against the plugin.
AudioPlayersMusicPlayer hands out one player per asset even when several callers ask for the same asset at the same time.
MusicService does not restart the current track when it is asked for it again, so the initial resumed notification cannot double the playback.
A foreground change pauses and resumes; only switching the channel off stops and resets.
test/music_service_test.dart proves that two overlapping starts create one player, and that a pause/resume cycle neither restarts the track nor advances it.
The whole suite stays green and flutter analyze reports no new issues on the pinned SDK.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The analyzer reports no new issues, the whole suite passes, and the new tests fail against the old code and pass against the new one. The on-device check is the same instrumented run that found the bug: after the fix, a single launch must log one prepared player and one start, and a return to the foreground must not log a fresh start.

Assumptions.Assumption: Two players for one track is audible as doubling and worth fixing even though the discarded first tree is torn down: the fade runs for 600 ms, which is long enough for both to be heard.
audioplayers' pause keeps the position, so resume continues the track; the plugin documents pause separately from stop, which resets to the beginning.
